title: Kenyan Vegetable Pasta
community: Urban Kenya — the vegetarian restaurant option
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Vegetable Pasta — penne or rigatoni tossed with roasted cherry tomatoes, courgette, spinach, garlic, olive oil, and parmesan in a light tomato-cream sauce. The vegetarian restaurant pasta that does not compromise.
longDesc: Vegetable pasta on a Kenyan restaurant menu is the dish that has improved dramatically as the country's food culture has evolved — roasted rather than boiled vegetables, a proper tomato-cream sauce, and quality parmesan make this genuinely satisfying.
steps: Roast cherry tomatoes at 200°C with olive oil and salt for 15 minutes.
Cook pasta al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Sauté courgette in olive oil and butter until golden — 4 minutes.
Add garlic and paprika. Cook 1 minute.
Add roasted tomatoes and cream. Simmer 3 minutes.
Add pasta and pasta water. Toss.
Add spinach. Toss until just wilted.
chefTips: Roasting the tomatoes first concentrates their flavour dramatically.
Add spinach only at the end — it wilts in seconds.
cookingScience: Roasting tomatoes at 200°C drives off 60—70% of their water content, concentrating sugars and acids while promoting Maillard browning of the sugars — producing intensely flavoured roasted tomatoes with far more depth than raw or boiled tomatoes.
sustainabilityTips: All vegetables locally grown in Kenya — lowest possible food miles.
reheating: Gently on stovetop with splash of water.
healthBenefits: Multiple vegetables provide vitamins and fibre.
Olive oil provides healthy monounsaturated fats.
culturalNote: Vegetable pasta demonstrates that Nairobi's restaurant scene now serves genuinely excellent vegetarian options — not an afterthought but a properly conceived, beautifully executed dish.
